lille.explanation: "Lille" means "small". To talk about more than one thing, use "små" (small), which looks different from "lille": "små biler" (small cars). To say someone is dear and little, say: "min lille ven" (my little friend).

lim.explanation: "Lim" means "glue". The verb is "at lime" (to glue): "Jeg limer billedet på papiret" (I glue the picture on the paper).

linser.explanation: "Linser" means "lentils". To say one lentil, use "en linse": "Der ligger en linse på gulvet" (There is a lentil on the floor). The same word also means a lens: "en kontaktlinse" (a contact lens).

litteratur.explanation: "Litteratur" means "literature". To say all that has been written about a subject, add "om" (about): "litteraturen om søvn" (the literature on sleep).

livlig.explanation: "Livlig" means "lively". Do not mix it up with "levende" (alive): "et levende dyr" (a living animal) is not dead, while "en livlig fest" (a lively party) is full of energy.

livsglæde.explanation: "En livsglæde" means "joy of life". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en glæde" (a joy). To say a person has it, use "livsglad" (full of joy of life): "Hun er livsglad" (She is full of joy of life).

livskvalitet.explanation: "Livskvalitet" means "quality of life". It is built from "et liv" (a life) and "en kvalitet" (a quality). To say a hobby makes your life better, say: "Hobbyen giver mig livskvalitet" (The hobby gives me quality of life).

logik.explanation: "Logik" means "logic". To say there is a reason behind something, say: "Der er en logik i det" (There is logic in it). The describing word is "logisk" (logical).

logisk.explanation: "Logisk" means "logical". It comes from "en logik" (logic). To say something makes sense, say: "Det er helt logisk" (That is completely logical).

lokal.explanation: "Lokal" means "local". To talk about news from your own town, say: "lokale nyheder" (local news).

lokalt.explanation: "Lokalt" means "locally". It comes from "lokal" (local). To say you buy things in your own area, put it after the verb: "Jeg handler lokalt" (I shop locally).

lommepenge.explanation: "Lommepenge" means "pocket money". It is built from "en lomme" (a pocket) and "penge" (money). The word "lomme" is also in "en lommelygte" (a flashlight): "Jeg har en lommelygte i tasken" (I have a flashlight in my bag).

lotto.explanation: "Lotto" means "lotto". In Denmark, "Lotto" is run by the company "Danske Spil".

lovende.explanation: "Lovende" means "promising". It comes from the verb "at love" (to promise). To say a person has talent, say: "Hun er et lovende talent" (She is a promising talent).

lovgivning.explanation: "Lovgivning" means "legislation". This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Dansk lovgivning gælder for alle" (Danish legislation applies to everyone). It is built from "en lov" (a law) and "at give" (to give).

lovlig.explanation: "Lovlig" means "legal". To say the opposite, put "u" in front: "ulovlig" (illegal). To say stealing is not allowed, say: "Det er ulovligt at stjæle" (It is illegal to steal).

lovpligtig.explanation: "Lovpligtig" means "legally required". It is built from "en lov" (a law) and "pligtig" (obliged). To say a thing is required by law, say: "Cykellygter er lovpligtige" (Bike lights are required by law).

loyal.explanation: "Loyal" means "loyal". To say who you are loyal to, add "over for" (towards): "Han er loyal over for sin chef" (He is loyal to his boss).

loyalitet.explanation: "Loyalitet" means "loyalty". The matching describing word is "loyal" (loyal): "en loyal ven" (a loyal friend).

luft.explanation: "Luft" means "air". To say something is in the air, say: "Fuglen er i luften" (The bird is in the air). It is also the first part of "en lufthavn" (an airport), literally "an air harbor".

lukket.explanation: "Lukket" means "closed". It comes from the verb "at lukke" (to close). To say a shop is not open, say: "Butikken er lukket" (The shop is closed).

luksus.explanation: "Luksus" means "luxury". To talk about something nice you do not need, say: "Et langt bad er luksus" (A long bath is a luxury).

lummer.explanation: "Lummer" means "muggy". For weather, use the form "lummert": "Vejret er lummert" (The weather is muggy). To say the weather is only hot, use "varm" (warm): "Det er en varm dag" (It is a warm day).

lun.explanation: "Lun" means "cozy". To say food or drink is nicely warm, use it for "warm": "lun suppe" (warm soup). To say someone has a gently dry sense of humor, say: "Han har en lun humor" (He has a gentle sense of humor).

ly.explanation: "Et ly" means "a shelter". To say you find a place to stay dry, say: "De fandt ly under et tag" (They found shelter under a roof). To say something happens hidden by darkness, use "i ly af mørket" (under cover of darkness): "Han sneg sig ind i ly af mørket" (He sneaked in under cover of darkness).
